verses.text: In the beginning, Yahawah created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was unformed and empty, darkness covered the deep waters, and the Spirit of Yahawah moved over the surface of the waters.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“Let there be light.”
And there was light.

verses.text: Yahawah saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness.
Yahawah called the light Day, and he called the darkness Night. Evening came, then morning—the first day.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“Let there be an expanse between the waters to separate water from water.”

verses.text: Yahawah made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above it. And it was so.
Yahawah called the expanse Sky. Evening came, then morning—the second day.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“Let the waters beneath the sky gather into one place, and let dry ground appear.”
And it was so.

verses.text: Yahawah called the dry ground Land, and the gathered waters Seas. Yahawah saw that it was good.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“Let the land produce vegetation:
plants that bear seed and fruit trees that bear fruit with
seed in it, each according to its kind.”
And it was so.

verses.text: The land produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants and trees bearing fruit with seed in it, each according to its kind. Yahawah saw that it was good.
Evening came, then morning—the third day.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“Let lights appear in the expanse of the sky to separate day from night. Let them mark appointed times, days, and years,
and let them shine from the sky upon the earth.”
And it was so.

verses.text: Yahawah made the two great lights: the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars.
Yahawah set them in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,
to govern the day and the night and to separate light from darkness. Yahawah saw that it was good.
Evening came, then morning—the fourth day.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the expanse of the sky.”

verses.text: Yahawah created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves and teems in the waters, each according to its kind, and every winged bird according to its kind. Yahawah saw that it was good.

parts.text: Yahawah blessed them, saying,
“Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply
on the earth.”

verses.text: Evening came, then morning—the fifth day.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals, each according to its kind.”
And it was so.

verses.text: Yahawah made the wild animals, the livestock, and everything that moves along the ground, each according to its kind. Yahawah saw that it was good.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,

“Let us make humanity in our image, according to our likeness. Let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the livestock, all the earth, and every creature that moves along the ground.”

verses.text: So Yahawah created humanity in his image; in the image of Yahawah he created them; male and female he created them.

parts.text: Yahawah blessed them and said to them,
“Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth and bring it under your care. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, and every living creature that moves on the earth.”
Then Yahawah said,
“Look, I have given you every seed-bearing plant across the earth and every tree with seed-bearing fruit. They will be food for you.
And to every wild animal, every bird of the sky, and everything that moves on the earth and has life, I have given every green plant for food.”
And it was so.

verses.text: Yahawah saw everything he had made, and it was very good. Evening came, then morning—the sixth day.
So the heavens and the earth were completed, together with everything in them.
By the seventh day Yahawah had completed the work he had done, and on the seventh day he ceased from all his work.
Yahawah blessed the seventh day and set it apart, because on that day he ceased from all the work of creation he had done.
This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, when Yahawah made the earth and the heavens.
No shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet grown, because Yahawah had not sent rain upon the earth and there was no human being to cultivate the ground.
But water rose from the earth and watered the entire surface of the ground.
Then Yahawah formed the man from dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
Yahawah planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and placed there the man he had formed.
Yahawah caused every tree that was pleasing to look at and good for food to grow from the ground. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided into four branches.
The name of the first is Pishon; it winds through the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold.
The gold of that land is good. Aromatic resin and onyx stone are also found there.
The name of the second river is Gihon; it winds through the entire land of Cush.
The name of the third river is Tigris; it flows east of Asshur. The fourth river is Euphrates.
Yahawah took the man and placed him in the garden of Eden to cultivate it and care for it.

parts.text: Yahawah commanded the man,
“You may freely eat from every tree in the garden,
but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of
good and evil, because on the day you eat from it, you
will certainly die.”
Then Yahawah said,
“It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper corresponding to him.”

verses.text: Yahawah formed from the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky. He brought them to the man to see what he would call them, and whatever the man called each living creature became its name.
The man gave names to all the livestock, the birds of the sky, and every wild animal. But no helper corresponding to the man was found for him.
So Yahawah caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. While he slept, Yahawah took one of his sides and closed the place with flesh.
Yahawah fashioned the side he had taken from the man into a woman and brought her to the man.
The man said, “At last, this is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh! She will be called Woman, because she was taken from Man.”
That is why a man leaves his father and mother and joins himself to his wife, and they become one flesh.
The man and his wife were both naked, but they felt no shame.
Now the serpent was more cunning than any wild animal Yahawah had made. He said to the woman, “Did Yahawah really say that you must not eat from any tree in the garden?”
The woman answered the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,
but Yahawah said about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, ‘You must not eat from it or touch it, or you will die.’”
The serpent said to the woman, “You will certainly not die.
Yahawah knows that when you eat from it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like the divine ones, knowing good and evil.”

The woman saw that the tree was good for food, pleasing to look at, and desirable for gaining wisdom. She took some of its fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate.
Then both their eyes were opened, and they knew they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
They heard the sound of Yahawah moving through the garden in the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hid among the trees of the garden from the presence of Yahawah.

parts.text: Yahawah called to the man and said,
“Where are you?”

verses.text: He answered, “I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid.”

parts.text: Yahawah said,
“Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?”

verses.text: The man answered, “The woman you gave to be with me gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.”

parts.text: Yahawah said to the woman,
“What have you done?”
The woman answered, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”
Then Yahawah said to the serpent,
“Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock and every wild animal. You will move on your belly and eat dust all
the days of your life.
I will place hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers. He will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.”
To the woman he said,
“I will greatly increase your pain in pregnancy; in pain you will give birth to children.
Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule
over you.”
To the man Yahawah said,
“Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree I commanded you not to
eat from, the ground is cursed because of you. Through
hard labor you will eat from it all the days of your life.
It will grow thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, because you were taken from it. You are dust, and to dust you will return.”

verses.text: The man named his wife Chawah, because she was the mother of all living.
Yahawah made garments of skin for the man and his wife and clothed them.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“The man has become like one of
us, knowing good and evil. Now he must not reach out,
take from the tree of life as well, eat, and live forever—”

verses.text: So Yahawah sent him out of the garden of Eden to cultivate the ground from which he had been taken.
He drove out the man and stationed the kerubim at the east of the garden of Eden, with a flaming sword turning in every direction to guard the way to the tree of life.
Now Adam knew his wife Chawah, and she conceived and gave birth to Qayin (Cain), saying, “I have received a man from Yahawah.”
Later, she gave birth to his brother Habal (Abel). Habal became a keeper of sheep, but Qayin worked the ground.
In the course of time, Qayin brought an offering to Yahawah from the fruit of the ground.
But Habal also brought an offering—the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. And Yahawah looked with favor on Habal and his offering,
but He did not regard Qayin and his offering. So Qayin became very angry, and his face fell.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said to Qayin,
“Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast?
If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door. It desires to have you, but you must rule over it.”

verses.text: Now Qayin said to his brother Habal, “Let’s go out to the field.” And while they were in the field, Qayin rose up against Habal his brother and killed him.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said to Qayin,
“Where is your brother Habal?”
Qayin answered, “I don’t know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
Yahawah said,
“What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.
Now you are cursed from the land, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its strength to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on
the earth.”

verses.text: Qayin said to Yahawah, “My punishment is too great to bear!
Today You are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from Your presence. I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”

parts.text: But Yahawah said to him,
“Not so! If anyone kills Qayin, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.”
And Yahawah put a mark on Qayin so that no one who found him would kill him.

verses.text: So Qayin went out from the presence of Yahawah and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Qayin knew his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Chanokh (Enoch). Then Qayin built a city and named it after his son, Chanokh.
To Chanokh was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mechuyael, and Mechuyael was the father of Methushael, and Methushael was the father of Lamek.
Lamek took two wives for himself: the name of the first was Adah, and the name of the second was Tsillah.
Adah gave birth to Yabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
His brother’s name was Yuval; he was the father of all who play the lyre and flute.
Tsillah also gave birth to Tubal-Qayin, who forged all kinds of tools from bronze and iron. The sister of Tubal-Qayin was Na’amah.
Then Lamek said to his wives: “Adah and Tsillah, listen to my voice, Wives of Lamek, hear my words. I have killed a man for wounding me, A young man for striking me.
If Qayin is avenged sevenfold, Then Lamek seventy-sevenfold.”
Adam again knew his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Shaṩath (Seth), saying, “Yahawah has given me another seed in place of Habal, since Qayin killed him.”
To Shaṩath also was born a son, and he called his name Enosh. At that time, men began to call upon the name of Yahawah.
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that Yahawah created man, He made him in the likeness of Elohim.
He created them male and female and blessed them. And He called their name Adam in the day they were created.
Adam lived 130 years and fathered a son in his own likeness, after his image, and he called his name Shaṩath (Seth).
After he fathered Shaṩath, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days that Adam lived were 930 years, and he died.
Shaṩath lived 105 years and fathered Enosh.
After he fathered Enosh, Shaṩath lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Shaṩath were 912 years, and he died.
Enosh lived 90 years and fathered Qeynan (Kenan).
After he fathered Qeynan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Enosh were 905 years, and he died.
Qeynan lived 70 years and fathered Mahalal’el.
After he fathered Mahalal’el, Qeynan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Qeynan were 910 years, and he died.
Mahalal’el lived 65 years and fathered Yared (Jared).
After he fathered Yared, Mahalal’el lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Mahalal’el were 895 years, and he died.
Yared lived 162 years and fathered Chanokh (Enoch).
After he fathered Chanokh, Yared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Yared were 962 years, and he died.
Chanokh lived 65 years and fathered Methushalach (Methuselah).
After he fathered Methushalach, Chanokh walked with Elohim for 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Chanokh were 365 years.
And Chanokh walked with Elohim, and he was not, for Yahawah took him.
Methushalach lived 187 years and fathered Lamek.
After he fathered Lamek, Methushalach lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Methushalach were 969 years, and he died.
Lamek lived 182 years and fathered a son.
And he called his name Noach (Noah), saying, “This one will bring us rest from our work and the toil of our hands, because of the ground that Yahawah has cursed.”
After he fathered Noach, Lamek lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
So all the days of Lamek were 777 years, and he died.
After Noach was 500 years old, he fathered Shem, Cham (Ham), and Yapheth (Japheth).
As people began to multiply across the earth and daughters were born to them,
The sons of Alahayam saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took wives for themselves, from whomever they chose.

parts.text: And Yahawah said,
“My Spirit will not strive with man
forever, for he is flesh; yet his days shall be one hundred
and twenty years.”

verses.text: The Naphalym (Nephilim) were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of Alahayam went in to the daughters of men and bore children to them. They were the mighty men of old, men of renown.
And Yahawah saw that the wickedness of man was great on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
And Yahawah regretted that He had made man on the earth, and it grieved Him in His heart.

parts.text: So Yahawah said,
“I will wipe away mankind, whom I have created, from the face of the earth—both man and beast, and creeping things, and birds of the heavens—for
I regret that I have made them.”

verses.text: But Noach found favor in the eyes of Yahawah.
This is the genealogy of Noach. Noach was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noach walked with Alahayam.
And Noach had three sons: Sham (Shem), Cham (Ham), and Yapheth (Japheth).
Now the earth was corrupt before Alahayam, and the earth was filled with violence.
And Alahayam looked upon the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.

parts.text: Then Alahayam said to Noach,
“The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. Behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms
in the ark, and coat it inside and outside with pitch.
And this is how you shall make it: The length of the ark
shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and
its height thirty cubits.
Make a roof for the ark, and finish it to within a cubit from the top. Set the door of the ark on its side, and make it with lower, second, and third decks.
And behold, I will bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh under the heavens in which there is the breath of life. Everything that is on the earth shall perish.
But I will establish My covenant with you, and you shall enter the ark—you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every kind
shall come to you to keep them alive, male and female.
Of the birds after their kind, of the beasts after their kind, and of every creeping thing on the ground after its kind, two of every kind shall come to you to keep them alive.
And take with you every kind of food that is eaten, and
store it away; it shall serve as food for you and for them.”

verses.text: And Noach did all that Alahayam commanded him, so he did.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said to Noach,
“Enter the ark, you and all your household, because I have seen that you are righteous before Me in this generation.
Take with you seven pairs of every clean beast, a male and its female, and two of every unclean beast, a male and its female.
Also take seven pairs of the birds of the heavens, male and female, to keep their offspring alive on the face of all
the earth.
For in seven days, I will cause it to rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe away every living thing that I have made from the face of the ground.”

verses.text: And Noach did all that Yahawah commanded him.
Noach was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
So Noach, his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.
Of the clean beasts and the unclean, of the birds, and of everything that creeps on the ground,
Two by two they came to Noach in the ark, male and female, as Alahayam had commanded Noach.
And after seven days, the waters of the flood came upon the earth.

In the six hundredth year of Noach’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that same day, Noach and his sons, Sham, Cham, and Yapheth, and Noach’s wife and the three wives of his sons, entered the ark.
They and every beast after its kind, all the livestock after their kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind—every fowl, every winged creature.
They came to Noach, into the ark, two by two of all flesh in which was the breath of life.
And those that entered, male and female of all flesh, went in as Alahayam had commanded him. Then Yahawah shut the door behind him.
The flood continued on the earth for forty days. The waters rose and lifted the ark, and it floated high above the earth.
The waters increased and prevailed greatly upon the earth, and the ark moved upon the surface of the waters.
And the waters overwhelmed the earth exceedingly, so that all the high mountains under the whole heavens were covered.
The waters rose fifteen cubits above the mountains and covered them.
And all flesh that moved upon the earth perished—birds, livestock, beasts, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and all mankind.
Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.

So Yahawah wiped out every living thing on the face of the earth—man and beast, creeping things, and birds of the heavens. They were all destroyed from the earth. Only Noach and those with him in the ark remained.
And the waters prevailed upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
And Alahayam remembered Noach and every living thing, and all the beasts that were with him in the ark. And Yahawah made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
The fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the heavens was restrained.
And the waters receded steadily from the earth. After one hundred and fifty days, the waters had gone down.
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
The waters continued to decrease until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains became visible.
At the end of forty days, Noach opened the window of the ark that he had made,
And he sent out a raven, which went back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
Then he sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the face of the ground.

But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, so she returned to him in the ark, for the waters were still covering the earth. So he reached out his hand, took her, and brought her back into the ark.
He waited another seven days, and again he sent out the dove from the ark.
And the dove came back to him in the evening, and behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noach knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
He waited yet another seven days and sent out the dove again, but she did not return to him anymore.

In the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the waters had dried up from the earth. And Noach removed the covering of the ark and looked, and behold, the surface of the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
Then Yahawah spoke to Noach, saying,

parts.text: “Come out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and their wives with you.
Bring out with you every living thing of all flesh—birds, beasts, and every creeping thing that moves
on the earth—so that they may multiply on the earth, be
fruitful, and increase in number.”

verses.text: So Noach went out, along with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives.
Every beast, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—came out of the ark, each according to its kind.
Then Noach built an altar to Yahawah, and he took of every clean beast and of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

parts.text: And Yahawah smelled the pleasing aroma, and Yahawah said in His heart,
“I will never again curse the ground because of man, even though the inclination of the heart of man is evil from his youth. Nor will I ever again destroy every living thing as I have done.
While the earth remains, Seedtime and harvest, Cold and heat, Summer and winter, Day and night, Shall not cease.”
And Yahawah blessed Noach and his sons, and He said to them,
“Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
The fear and dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, every bird of the heavens, everything that moves on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. Into your hands they are given.
Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you; just
as I gave you the green plants, I now give you all things.
But you must not eat flesh with its lifeblood still in it.
And surely I will require the blood of your lives; at the hand of every beast I will require it, and at the hand of man. At the hand of every man’s brother I will require the life of man.
Whoever sheds the blood of man, By man his blood shall be shed, For in the image of Alahayam, He made man.
But as for you, be fruitful and multiply; Bring forth abundantly on the earth, And increase in number upon it.”

verses.text: Then Yahawah spoke to Noach and to his sons with him, saying,

parts.text: “Behold, I establish My covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
And with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth that came
out of the ark with you—every living thing of the earth.
I establish My covenant with you: Never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood, and never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
And Yahawah said,
“This is the sign of the covenant that I make between Me and you, and every living creature that is with you, for all generations to come:
I have set My bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of
the covenant between Me and the earth.
Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the bow is seen in the clouds,
I will remember My covenant, which is between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh. And the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
When the bow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between Alahayam and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
So Yahawah said to Noach,
“This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and all flesh
that is on the earth.” The Sons of Noach and the Curse

verses.text: The sons of Noach who came out of the ark were Sham, Cham, and Yapheth. Cham was the father of Kanaan.
These three were the sons of Noach, and from them the whole earth was repopulated.
Now Noach, a man of the soil, was the first to plant a vineyard.
And he drank of the wine and became drunk, and he lay uncovered inside his tent.
Cham, the father of Kanaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brothers outside.

But Sham and Yapheth took a garment, laid it across their shoulders, and walking backward, they covered their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned away so they did not see their father’s nakedness.
When Noach awoke from his wine and learned what his youngest son had done to him,
He said, “Cursed be Kanaan! A servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.”
He also said, “Blessed be Yahawah the Alahayam of Sham! And let Kanaan be his servant.
May Alahayam enlarge Yapheth, And may he dwell in the tents of Sham, And let Kanaan be his servant.”
After the flood, Noach lived 350 years.
So all the days of Noach were 950 years, and then he died.
Now these are the generations of the sons of Noach: Sham, Cham, and Yapheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Yapheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Yawan, Tubal, Meshek, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Yawan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
From these, the coastland peoples spread out into their lands, each with their own language, by their clans, in their nations.
The sons of Cham: Kush, Mitsrayim, Put, and Kanaan.
The sons of Kush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteka. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Kush fathered Nimrod, who became a mighty one on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before Yahawah; therefore it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before Yahawah.”
The first centers of his kingdom were Babel, Erek, Akkad, and Kalneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land, he went to Asshur and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Kalhu,
And Resen, between Nineveh and Kalhu, which is the great city.
Mitsrayim fathered: Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Kasluhim (from whom came the Pelishtim), and Kaphtorim.
Kanaan fathered: Tsidon, his firstborn, and Chet,
The Yebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite,
The Chiwwite, the Arqite, the Sinite,
The Arwadite, the Tsemarite, and the Chamathite. Afterward, the clans of the Kanaanites spread abroad.
And the border of the Kanaanites extended from Tsidon toward Gerar, as far as Azzah (Gaza), and toward Sedom, Amorah, Admah, and Tseboyim, as far as Lasha.
These were the sons of Cham, by their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
Sham, the elder brother of Yapheth, also had children. He was the father of all the children of Eber.
The sons of Sham: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram: Utz, Chul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad fathered Shelach, and Shelach fathered Eber.
To Eber, two sons were born: The name of one was Peleg, because in his days, the earth was divided, And his brother’s name was Yoqtan.
Yoqtan fathered: Almodad, Sheleph, Chatzarmaveth, Yerach,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diqlah,
Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Yobab. All these were sons of Yoqtan.
Their territory extended from Mesha toward Sephar, the eastern hill country.
These were the sons of Sham, by their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
These were the clans of the sons of Noach, according to their genealogies, in their nations. From them the nations spread across the earth after the flood.
And the whole earth had one language and one speech.
And as they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they dwelt there.
Then they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and burn them thoroughly.” And they had brick for stone, and they had tar for mortar.
Then they said, “Come, let us build for ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered over the face of the whole earth.”
But Yahawah came down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men had built.

parts.text: And Yahawah said,
“Behold, the people are one, and they all have one language, and this they begin to do. Now nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.
Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they do not understand one another’s speech.”

verses.text: So Yahawah scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they ceased building the city.
Therefore its name is called Babel, because there Yahawah confused the language of all the earth; and from there Yahawah scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.
These are the generations of Shem. Shem was 100 years old and fathered Arpachshad two years after the flood.
And Shem lived after he fathered Arpachshad 500 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Arpachshad lived 35 years and fathered Shelah.
And Arpachshad lived after he fathered Shelah 403 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Shelah lived 30 years and fathered Eber.
And Shelah lived after he fathered Eber 403 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Eber lived 34 years and fathered Peleg.
And Eber lived after he fathered Peleg 430 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Peleg lived 30 years and fathered Reu.
And Peleg lived after he fathered Reu 209 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Reu lived 32 years and fathered Serug.
And Reu lived after he fathered Serug 207 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Serug lived 30 years and fathered Nahor.
And Serug lived after he fathered Nahor 200 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Nahor lived 29 years and fathered Terah.
And Nahor lived after he fathered Terah 119 years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And Terah lived 70 years and fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Now these are the generations of Terah. Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran fathered Lot.
And Haran died before his father Terah in the land of his nativity, in Ur of the Chaldees.
And Abram and Nahor took wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife, Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and Iscah.
But Sarai was barren; she had no child.

And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot, the son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram’s wife, and they went forth together from Ur of the Chaldees to go into the land of Canaan. And they came to Haran and dwelt there.
And the days of Terah were 205 years, and Terah died in Haran.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said to Abram,
“Leave your land, your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.
I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be a blessing.
I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse those who curse you. Through you, all the families of the earth will be blessed.”

verses.text: So Abram departed as Yahawah commanded him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all their possessions and people they had acquired in Haran. Then they set out for the land of Kanaan, and they arrived there.
Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of Shekem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time, the Kanaanites were still in the land.

parts.text: Then Yahawah appeared to Abram and said,
“To your seed I will give this land.”
So Abram built an altar there to Yahawah, who had appeared to him.

verses.text: From there, he moved on to the hill country east of Bayath-Al (Bethel) and pitched his tent, with Bayath-Al to the west and Ay to the east. There he built another altar to Yahawah and called on His Name.
Then Abram continued his journey by stages toward the Negeb.
Now a famine struck the land, so Abram went down to Mitsrayim to stay there for a while, because the famine was severe.
As he was about to enter Mitsrayim, he said to his wife Sarai, “Listen, I know you are a beautiful woman.
When the Mitsrayim see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife,’ and they will kill me but let you live.
Please say you are my sister, so that it will go well for me because of you, and my life will be spared because of you.”
When Abram entered Mitsrayim, the Mitsrayim saw that Sarai was a very beautiful woman.
Pharaoh’s officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, so she was taken into his house.
Because of Sarai, Pharaoh treated Abram well, and he received sheep, cattle, male and female donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.
But Yahawah struck Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
So Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, “What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now, here is your wife—take her and go!”
Then Pharaoh gave orders to his men concerning Abram, and they sent him away with his wife and all he had.
So Abram went up from Mitsrayim (Egypt) to the Negeb, he and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him.
Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.
He journeyed by stages from the Negeb back to Bayath-Al (Bethel), to the place where his tent had been at first, between Bayath-Al and Ay,
To the place of the altar that he had built there at first. And there Abram called on the Name of Yahawah.
Now Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.
But the land could not support both of them dwelling together, because their possessions were so great that they could not stay in the same place.
And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. (At that time, the Kanaanites and Perizzites were also dwelling in the land.)
So Abram said to Lot, “Please, let there be no strife between you and me, or between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are brothers.
Is not the whole land before you? Please separate from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.”

Lot looked up and saw that the entire plain of the Yarden (Jordan) was well-watered everywhere—before Yahawah destroyed Sodom and Amorah (Gomorrah)—like the garden of Yahawah, like the land of Mitsrayim, as far as Tsoar.
So Lot chose for himself the entire plain of the Yarden, and Lot journeyed eastward. They separated from each other.
Abram dwelt in the land of Kanaan, while Lot dwelt among the cities of the plain and pitched his tents near Sodom.
Now the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinful against Yahawah.

parts.text: After Lot had separated from him, Yahawah said to Abram,
“Lift up your eyes now and look from the place where you are—northward, southward, eastward, and westward.
For all the land that you see, I will give to you and your seed forever.
And I will make your seed as the dust of the earth, so that if anyone can count the dust of the earth, then your seed could also be counted.
Arise, walk through the land, its length and its width, for I am giving it to you.”

verses.text: So Abram moved his tent and dwelt by the oaks of Mamre in Hebron, and there he built an altar to Yahawah.
In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyam,
They waged war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsah king of Amorah (Gomorrah), Shinab king of Admah, Shember king of Tseboyim, and the king of Bela (Tsoar).
All these joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, which is the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they had served Kedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year, they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year, Kedorlaomer and the kings with him came and defeated the Rephaim in Ashteroth-Qarnayim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh-Qiryathayim,
And the Horites in their mountain of Seir, as far as El-Paran, which is by the wilderness.
Then they turned back and came to En-Mishpat (Qadesh), and they struck all the country of the Amalekites and also the Amorites who dwelt in Hazazon-Tamar.
Then the king of Sodom, the king of Amorah, the king of Admah, the king of Tseboyim, and the king of Bela (Tsoar) went out and joined battle in the Valley of Siddim
Against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goyam, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar— four kings against five.
Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Amorah fled, some fell into them, while the rest fled to the mountains.
So the four kings seized all the goods of Sodom and Amorah, and all their food supply, and went on their way.
They also took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who was living in Sodom, along with his possessions, and departed.
But one who escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. He was dwelling by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshkol and Aner, who were allies of Abram.
When Abram heard that his relative had been taken captive, he mustered his trained men, born in his household—318 of them—and pursued them as far as Dan.
He divided his forces against them at night—he and his servants—and defeated them, pursuing them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
He recovered all the goods and also brought back his relative Lot, along with his possessions, as well as the women and the people.
After Abram returned from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh (the King’s Valley).
Then Malki-Tsedeq king of Shalam (Salem), brought out bread and wine—he was a priest of Alahayam Most High.
And he blessed him, saying: “Blessed be Abram by Alahayam Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
And blessed be Alahayam Most High, Who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
Then the king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, but take the goods for yourself.”
But Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have sworn to Yahawah, Alahayam Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
That I will not take a thread, or a sandal strap, or anything that belongs to you, so that you will not say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
I will take nothing except what the young men have eaten and the share that belongs to the men who went with me—Aner, Eshkol, and Mamre. Let them take their portion.”

parts.text: After these things, the word of Yahawah came to Abram in a vision, saying,
“Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, Your exceedingly great reward.”

verses.text: But Abram said, “O Yahawah Alahayam, what will You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?”
Then Abram said, “Look, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir.”

parts.text: Then the word of Yahawah came to him, saying,
“This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.”
Then He brought him outside and said,
“Look now toward the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to number them.”
And He said to him,
“So shall your descendants be.”

verses.text: And Abram believed Yahawah, and it was counted to him as righteousness.

parts.text: Then He said to him,
“I am Yahawah, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to inherit it.”

verses.text: But Abram said, “O Yahawah Alahayam, how will I know that I shall inherit it?”

parts.text: So He said to him,
“Bring Me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”

verses.text: Then Abram brought all these to Him, cut them in two, and placed each half opposite the other, but he did not cut the birds.
Then the birds of prey came down upon the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
As the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and behold, great darkness and terror fell upon him.

parts.text: Then Yahawah said to Abram:
“Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs. They will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation they serve, And afterward they will come out with great possessions.
You, however, will go to your fathers in peace, And be buried at a good old age.
In the fourth generation they shall return here, For the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”

verses.text: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces.

parts.text: On that day, Yahawah made a covenant with Abram, saying:
“To your descendants I have given this land, From the river of Mitsrayim to the great river, the Euphrates—
The land of the Qeynite, the Qenizzite, the Qadmonite,
The Hittite, the Perizzite, the Rephaim,
The Amorite, the Kanaanite, the Girgashite, and the Yebusite.”

verses.text: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. But she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.
So Sarai said to Abram, “Look, Yahawah has restrained me from bearing children. Please, go into my maidservant; perhaps I shall obtain children by her.” And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
So after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Kanaan, Sarai took Hagar, her Egyptian maidservant, and gave her to Abram as his wife.
And he went into Hagar, and she conceived. But when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress became despised in her eyes.

Then Sarai said to Abram, “My wrong be upon you! I gave my maidservant into your embrace, and when she saw that she had conceived, I became despised in her eyes. May Yahawah judge between you and me!”
But Abram said to Sarai, “Look, your maid is in your hands; do to her as you see fit.” Then Sarai dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her presence.
Now the Angel of Yahawah found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, the spring on the way to Shur.
And He said, “Hagar, Sarai’s maid, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She replied, “I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai.”
Then the Angel of Yahawah said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hand.”
And the Angel of Yahawah said, “I will greatly multiply your descendants, so that they will be too numerous to count.”
And the Angel of Yahawah said to her: “Behold, you are pregnant, and you shall bear a son, And you shall call his name Yishma’al (Ishmael), Because Yahawah has heard your affliction.
He will be a wild man; His hand will be against every man, And every man’s hand against him. And he shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers.”
Then she called the name of Yahawah who spoke to her, “You are El-Ro’i,” for she said, “Have I also seen Him who sees me?”
Therefore the well was called Be’er-Lachai-Ro’i; it is between Qadesh and Bered.
So Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named his son Yishma’al.
Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Yishma’al to him.

parts.text: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, Yahawah appeared to him and said,
“I am Alahayam Almighty. Walk before Me and be perfect.
I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”

verses.text: Then Abram fell on his face, and Yahawah spoke with him, saying,

parts.text: “As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you, and you shall be the father of many nations.
No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abaraham (Abraham), For I have made you a father of many nations.
I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come from you.
And I will establish My covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you, throughout their generations, for an everlasting covenant— to be Alahayam to you and to your seed after you.
I will give to you and to your descendants after you the land where you are a stranger— all the land of Kanaan—as an everlasting possession, and I will be their Alahayam.”
Then Yahawah said to Abaraham,
“As for you, you shall keep My covenant, you and your descendants after you throughout their generations.
This is My covenant, which you shall keep between Me and you and your seed after you: Every male among you shall be circumcised.
You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskins, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.
Every male among you who is eight days old shall be circumcised, every male in your generations—whether born in your house or bought with money from any foreigner who is not of your seed.
Both he who is born in your house and he who is bought with your money must be circumcised. My covenant shall be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
And any uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin shall be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.”
Then Yahawah said to Abaraham,
“As for your wife Sarai, you shall not call her name Sarai, but her name shall be Sarah.
I will bless her, and I will also give you a son by her. Yes, I will bless her, and she shall become a mother of nations; kings of peoples shall come from her.”

verses.text: Then Abaraham fell on his face and laughed, saying in his heart, “Shall a child be born to a man who is one hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?”
And Abaraham said to Yahawah, “Oh, that Yishma’al might live before You!”

parts.text: But Yahawah said,
“No, Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Yatadzaq (Yitzhaq / Isaac). I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
As for Yishma’al, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He shall father twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
But My covenant I will establish with Yatadzaq, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this set time next year.”

verses.text: When Yahawah had finished speaking with him, He went up from Abaraham.

So Abaraham took Yishma’al his son, and all who were born in his house and bought with his money—every male among the men of Abaraham’s household—and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very same day, as Yahawah had commanded him.
Abaraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised.
Yishma’al his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised.
That very day, Abaraham and his son Yishma’al were circumcised.
And all the men of his household—whether born in the house or bought with money from a foreigner—were circumcised with him.
Then Yahawah appeared to Abaraham by the oaks of Mamre, as he was sitting at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.
He lifted his eyes and looked, and behold, three men were standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the tent door to meet them and bowed himself to the ground,
and said, “Yahawah, if I have found favor in Your sight, do not pass by Your servant.
Please let a little water be brought to wash Your feet, and rest Yourselves under the tree.
I will bring You a piece of bread, that You may refresh Yourselves, and after that, You may go on—since You have come to Your servant.” And they said, “Do as you have said.”
So Abaraham hurried into the tent to Sarah and said, “Quick! Knead three measures of fine flour and make bread.”
Then Abaraham ran to the herd, took a tender and good calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
He took curds, milk, and the calf that he had prepared, and set it before them. And he stood by them under the tree while they ate.
Then they said to him, “Where is Sarah, your wife?” And he said, “There, in the tent.”

parts.text: Then Yahawah said,
“I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife shall have a son.”
Now Sarah was listening at the tent door behind him.

verses.text: Abaraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in years, and Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
So Sarah laughed to herself, saying, “After I have grown old, shall I have pleasure, and my master is also old?”

parts.text: Then Yahawah said to Abaraham,
“Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Shall I indeed bear a child, now that I am old?’
Is anything too hard for Yahawah? At the appointed time, I will return to you, and Sarah shall have a son.”
But Sarah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh,” for she was afraid. But He said,
“No, you did laugh.”

verses.text: Then the men arose from there and looked toward Sodom, and Abaraham walked with them to send them on their way.

parts.text: And Yahawah said,
“Shall I hide from Abaraham what I am about to do,
Since Abaraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

For I have chosen him, that he may command his children and his household after him to keep the way of Yahawah by doing righteousness and justice—so that Yahawah may bring to Abaraham what He has promised him.”
Then Yahawah said,
“The outcry against Sodom and Amorah is great, and their sin is very grave.
I will go down now and see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry that has come to Me. If not, I will know.”

verses.text: Then the men turned away from there and went toward Sodom, but Abaraham remained standing before Yahawah.
Abaraham approached and said, “Will You indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city. Will You indeed sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are in it?

Far be it from You to do such a thing—to slay the righteous with the wicked—so that the righteous should be treated like the wicked! Far be it from You! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”

parts.text: And Yahawah said,
“If I find fifty righteous within the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.”

verses.text: Then Abaraham answered and said, “Behold, I have undertaken to speak to Yahawah, I who am but dust and ashes.

parts.text: Suppose five of the fifty righteous are lacking. Will You destroy the whole city for lack of five?” And He said,
“If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.”
Again, he spoke to Him and said, “Suppose forty are found there?” And He said,
“I will not do it for the sake of forty.”
Then he said, “Let not Yahawah be angry, and I will speak. Suppose thirty are found there?” And He said,
“I will not do it if I find thirty there.”
He said, “Behold, I have undertaken to speak to Yahawah. Suppose twenty are found there?” And He said,
“I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.”
Then he said, “Let not Yahawah be angry, and I will speak but once more. Suppose ten are found there?” And He said,
“I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.”

verses.text: Then Yahawah went on His way when He had finished speaking to Abaraham, and Abaraham returned to his place.
The two messengers came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he rose to meet them and bowed himself with his face to the ground.

And he said, “My masters, please turn aside into your servant’s house. Spend the night and wash your feet. Then you may rise early and go on your way.” But they said, “No, we will spend the night in the open square.”
But Lot insisted strongly, so they turned aside to him and entered his house. Then he made them a feast and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Before they had gone to bed, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, both young and old, surrounded the house.
And they called to Lot and said, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them carnally.”
So Lot went out to them at the doorway, shutting the door behind him,
and said, “Please, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing!

See now, I have two daughters who have never known a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them as you please. But do nothing to these men, for they have come under the protection of my roof.”

But they said, “Stand back!” And they said, “This man came to stay here as a foreigner, and now he dares to judge us! We will deal worse with you than with them.” And they pressed hard against Lot and came near to break down the door.
But the men inside reached out their hands, pulled Lot into the house, and shut the door.
Then they struck the men at the entrance of the house, both young and old, with blindness, so that they could not find the door.
Then the men said to Lot, “Have you anyone else here? Sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you—get them out of this place!
For we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against its people has grown so great before Yahawah that He has sent us to destroy it.”

So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters, and said, “Get up! Leave this place, for Yahawah is about to destroy the city!” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.
As morning dawned, the messengers urged Lot, saying, “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city!”
But Lot hesitated, so the men seized his hand, the hands of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters—because Yahawah had mercy on him—and they brought him out and set him outside the city.
As soon as they had brought them out, one of them said, “Escape for your life! Do not look behind you, nor stop anywhere in the plain! Escape to the mountains, or you will be swept away!”
But Lot said to them, “Please, no, my master!
You have shown kindness to Your servant and have magnified Your mercy in saving my life, but I cannot escape to the mountains—lest disaster overtake me and I die.
Look, there is a small city nearby where I can flee—it is a little one. Let me escape there, and my life will be spared.”
So He said to him, “Very well, I will grant you this favor also: I will not overthrow the city you have spoken of.
Hurry! Escape there quickly, for I cannot do anything until you arrive there.” Therefore, the name of the city was called Tso’ar.
By the time Lot reached Tso’ar, the sun had risen over the land.
Then Yahawah rained down fire and sulfur from the heavens upon Sodom and Amorah.
And He overthrew those cities, the entire plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and everything that grew on the ground.
But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
Early the next morning, Abaraham got up and went to the place where he had stood before Yahawah.
He looked down toward Sodom and Amorah and all the land of the plain, and he saw thick smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace.
So it was that when Alahayam destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abaraham and sent Lot out of the midst of the destruction, when He overthrew the cities in which Lot had lived.
Then Lot went up from Tso’ar and settled in the mountains with his two daughters, because he was afraid to stay in Tso’ar. So he and his two daughters lived in a cave.
One day, the older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to give us children as is the custom of the earth.
Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him so that we may preserve our father’s lineage.”
So that night they made their father drink wine, and the older daughter went in and lay with her father. But he was unaware of when she lay down or when she arose.

The next day, the older daughter said to the younger, “Last night, I lay with my father. Let us make him drink wine again tonight, so you may go in and lie with him, that we may preserve our father’s lineage.”
So they made their father drink wine that night as well, and the younger daughter went and lay with him. But again, he was unaware of when she lay down or when she arose.
Thus both of Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab; he became the ancestor of the Moabites to this day.
The younger daughter also gave birth to a son and named him Ben-Ammi; he became the ancestor of the Ammonites to this day.
Abaraham journeyed from there toward the land of the Negev and dwelt between Qadesh and Shur. Then he sojourned in Gerar.
And Abaraham said of Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
But Alahayam came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him, “Behold, you are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken, for she is a man’s wife.”
Now Abimelech had not gone near her, so he said, “Master, will You slay a righteous nation even though I am innocent?
Did he not himself say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this with a pure heart and clean hands.”
And Alahayam said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this with a pure heart. That is why I withheld you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now therefore, restore the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not restore her, know that you shall surely die, you and all who belong to you.”
So Abimelech rose early in the morning and called all his servants, and told them all these things. And the men were greatly afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abaraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought such great guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should never be done!”
Then Abimelech asked Abaraham, “What was your reasoning, that you did this thing?”
Abaraham replied, “Because I thought, ‘Surely there is no fear of Alahayam in this place, and they will kill me on account of my wife.’
And besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father, though not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.
And when Alahayam caused me to wander from my father’s house, I said to her, ‘This is the kindness you must show me: At every place we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
Then Abimelech took sheep, cattle, and male and female servants, and gave them to Abaraham. And he restored Sarah, his wife, to him.
And Abimelech said, “Behold, my land is before you. Settle wherever it pleases you.”
To Sarah he said, “Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. This is a sign of your vindication before all who are with you; you are completely cleared.”
Then Abaraham prayed to Alahayam, and Alahayam healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, so they were able to bear children again.
For Yahawah had completely closed all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abaraham’s wife.
And Yahawah visited Sarah as He had said, and Yahawah did for Sarah as He had promised.
So Sarah conceived and bore Abaraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time that Alahayam had spoken to him.
And Abaraham called the name of his son who was born to him—whom Sarah bore to him—Yatsaḥaq.
Then Abaraham circumcised his son Yatsaḥaq when he was eight days old, just as Alahayam had commanded him.
Now Abaraham was one hundred years old when his son Yatsaḥaq was born to him.
And Sarah said, “Alahayam has made me laugh, and everyone who hears will laugh with me.”
She also said, “Who would have said to Abaraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”
So the child grew and was weaned, and Abaraham made a great feast on the day Yatsaḥaq was weaned.
But Sarah saw the son of Hagar, the Mitsrayam (Egyptian), whom she had borne to Abaraham, mocking.
So she said to Abaraham, “Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Yatsaḥaq.”
Now the matter was very grievous in Abaraham’s sight because of his son.
But Alahayam said to Abaraham, “Do not be distressed because of the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything Sarah tells you, for through Yatsaḥaq shall your seed be called.
Yet I will also make a nation of the son of the maidservant, because he is your offspring.”

So Abaraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave it to Hagar. He placed the child on her shoulder and sent her away. And she departed and wandered in the wilderness of Be’er-Sheba.
When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.
Then she went and sat down opposite him, a bowshot away, for she said, “Let me not see the death of the child.” And as she sat opposite him, she lifted up her voice and wept.

And Alahayam heard the voice of the boy. Then the messenger of Alahayam called to Hagar from the heavens and said to her, “What is troubling you, Hagar? Do not fear, for Alahayam has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
Arise, lift up the boy, and take hold of him with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”
Then Alahayam opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
And Alahayam was with the boy, and he grew. He lived in the wilderness and became a skilled archer.
He dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Mitsrayam.
Now it came to pass at that time that Abimelech and Phikol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abaraham, saying, “Alahayam is with you in all that you do.

Now therefore, swear to me here before Alahayam that you will not deal falsely with me, or with my children, or with my descendants. Show to me and the land where you have sojourned the same kindness I have shown to you.”
And Abaraham said, “I swear it.”
But Abaraham rebuked Abimelech because of a well of water that Abimelech’s servants had seized.
And Abimelech said, “I do not know who has done this; you did not tell me, nor have I heard of it until today.”
So Abaraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
Then Abaraham set seven ewe lambs apart from the flock.
And Abimelech asked Abaraham, “What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set apart?”
And he replied, “You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as a witness that I dug this well.”
That place was called Be’er-Sheba, because there the two men swore an oath.
So they made a covenant at Be’er-Sheba, and then Abimelech and Phikol, the commander of his army, arose and returned to the land of the Philistines.
Then Abaraham planted a tamarisk tree in Be’er-Sheba, and there he called upon the name of Yahawah, the Everlasting Alahayam.
And Abaraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
Now it came to pass after these things that Alahayam tested Abaraham and said to him, “Abaraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
Then Yahawah said, “Take your son, your only son Yatsaḥaq, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”

So Abaraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, along with his son Yatsaḥaq. He split wood for the burnt offering and set out for the place that Alahayam had told him about.
On the third day, Abaraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from afar.
Then Abaraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will return to you.”
So Abaraham took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it on his son Yatsaḥaq. He carried the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them walked on together.

Then Yatsaḥaq spoke to Abaraham his father and said, “My father?” And Abaraham replied, “Here I am, my son.” Then Yatsaḥaq said, “Behold, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
Abaraham answered, “My son, Yahawah will provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt offering.” And the two of them walked on together.
When they arrived at the place that Yahawah had told him about, Abaraham built an altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Yatsaḥaq and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Then Abaraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slay his son.
But the messenger of Yahawah called out to him from the heavens, saying, “Abaraham! Abaraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
Then Yahawah said, “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear Alahayam, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from Me.”
Then Abaraham lifted up his eyes and saw behind him a ram caught in the thicket by its horns. So Abaraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
And Abaraham called the name of that place Yahawah-Yireh(Yahawah Will Provide), as it is said to this day, “On the mountain of Yahawah, it shall be provided.”
Then the messenger of Yahawah called to Abaraham a second time from the heavens,
And said, “By Myself I have sworn, declares Yahawah, because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son,
I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your seed like the stars of the heavens and like the sand on the seashore. And your seed shall possess the gate of their enemies.
And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”
Then Abaraham returned to his young men, and they arose and went together to Be’er-Sheba. And Abaraham dwelt in Be’er-Sheba.
Now it came to pass after these things that it was reported to Abaraham, saying, “Milkah also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Qemuel the father of Aram,
Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Yidlaph, and Bethuel.”
And Bethuel fathered Ribqah (Rebekah). These eight Milkah bore to Nahor, Abaraham’s brother.
And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Ma’akah.
Now Sarah lived 127 years; these were the years of Sarah’s life.
And Sarah died in Qiryath-Arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Kanaan. And Abaraham mourned for Sarah and wept over her.
Then Abaraham arose from before his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
“I am a foreigner and a sojourner among you. Give me a burial site among you, so that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
And the sons of Heth answered Abaraham, saying to him,
“Listen to us, my master. You are a mighty prince among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb from you, so that you may bury your dead.”
Then Abaraham arose and bowed down to the people of the land, the sons of Heth.
And he spoke with them, saying, “If you are willing for me to bury my dead out of my sight, listen to me and speak to Ephron, son of Tsohar, on my behalf,
That he may give me the cave of Makhpelah, which he owns, which is at the end of his field. Let him give it to me at full price as a burial site among you.”
Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth; and Ephron the Hittite answered Abaraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth and all who entered the gate of his city, saying,
“No, my master, listen to me. I give you the field and the cave that is in it. In the presence of my people, I give it to you. Bury your dead.”
Then Abaraham bowed himself before the people of the land.

And he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, “If you will, please listen to me. I will pay you the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there.”
And Ephron answered Abaraham, saying to him,
“My master, listen to me. The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver. What is that between you and me? Bury your dead.”

So Abaraham listened to Ephron, and Abaraham weighed out to Ephron the silver that he had spoken in the hearing of the sons of Heth—four hundred shekels of silver, according to the weight current among the merchants.
So the field of Ephron in Makhpelah, which was near Mamre—the field and the cave in it, and all the trees within its borders—
Became Abaraham’s possession before the sons of Heth, before all who entered the gate of his city.
And after this, Abaraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field of Makhpelah, near Mamre (that is, Hebron), in the land of Kanaan.
So the field and the cave in it were deeded to Abaraham as a burial site by the sons of Heth.
Now Abaraham was old, well advanced in years, and Yahawah had blessed Abaraham in all things.
So Abaraham said to his servant, the oldest of his household, who managed all that he had, “Place your hand under my thigh,
And I will make you swear by Yahawah, the Alahayam of the heavens and the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kanaanites, among whom I dwell.
Instead, you shall go to my land and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son Yatschaq.”
But the servant said to him, “What if the woman is not willing to follow me to this land? Should I then take your son back to the land from which you came?”
And Abaraham said to him, “See to it that you do not take my son back there.

Yahawah, the Alahayam of the heavens, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my kindred, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘To your seed I will give this land,’ He will send His messenger before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
But if the woman is unwilling to follow you, then you will be released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there.”
So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of Abaraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.
Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed, taking all kinds of gifts from his master’s goods. And he arose and went to Aram-Naharaim, to the city of Nachor.
And he made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at evening time, when the women go out to draw water.
Then he said, “O Yahawah, Alahayam of my master Abaraham, please grant me success today, and show loving-kindness to my master Abaraham.
Behold, I stand by this well of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

Let it be that the young woman to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and she replies, ‘Drink, and I will also water your camels’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Yatschaq. And by this, I will know that You have shown loving-kindness to my master.”
And before he had finished speaking, behold, Ribqah (Rebekah) came out with her jar upon her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethu’el, son of Milkah, the wife of Nachor, Abaraham’s brother.
The young woman was very beautiful, a maiden who had never known a man. She went down to the well, filled her jar, and came up.
Then the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me drink a little water from your jar.”
And she said, “Drink, my master.” And she quickly let down her jar upon her hand and gave him a drink.
And when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will also draw water for your camels until they have finished drinking.”
Then she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran again to the well to draw water, and she drew for all his camels.
The man watched her closely, holding his peace to determine whether Yahawah had made his journey successful or not.
And when the camels had finished drinking, he took a golden nose ring weighing a half-sheqel, and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten sheqels of gold.
And he said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to lodge?”
And she said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethu’el, the son of Milkah, whom she bore to Nachor.”
Then she said, “We have both straw and fodder in abundance, and room to lodge.”
Then the man bowed his head and worshiped Yahawah,

And he said, “Blessed be Yahawah, Alahayam of my master Abaraham, who has not forsaken His loving-kindness and His truth toward my master. As for me, Yahawah has led me on the way to the house of my master’s relatives.”
Then the young woman ran and told her mother’s household these things.
Now Ribqah had a brother named Laban, and Laban ran out to the man at the well.

And it came to pass when he saw the nose ring and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of his sister Ribqah, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” that he went to the man and found him standing by the camels at the well.
And he said, “Come in, O blessed of Yahawah!Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”
So the man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels and provided straw and fodder for them, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
But when food was set before him to eat, he said, “I will not eat until I have stated my business.” And they said, “Speak on.”
And he said, “I am Abaraham’s servant.
Yahawah has greatly blessed my master, and he has become great. He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
And Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old, and to him he has given all that he has.
Now my master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kanaanites, in whose land I dwell,
But you shall go to my father’s house and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son.’”
I asked my master, “What if the woman will not follow me?”
He told me, “Yahawah, before whom I walk, will send his messenger with you and make your journey successful. You shall take a wife for my son from my family and my father’s house.
You will be released from my oath when you go to my family. If they will not give her to you, you will be released from my oath.”
I came to the spring today and said, “Yahawah, Alahayam of my master Abaraham, if you will make this journey successful,
I am standing by the spring of water. Let the young woman who comes out to draw water be the one to whom I say, ‘Please give me a little water from your jar,’
and who answers, ‘Drink, and I will draw water for your camels too.’ Let her be the woman Yahawah has appointed for my master’s son.”
Before I had finished speaking in my heart, Ribqah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. I said to her, “Please let me drink.”
She quickly lowered her jar and said, “Drink, and I will water your camels too.” So I drank, and she also watered the camels.
I asked her, “Whose daughter are you?” She said, “The daughter of Bethu’el, son of Nachor, whom Milkah bore to him.” Then I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.
I bowed down and worshiped Yahawah and blessed Yahawah, Alahayam of my master Abaraham, who led me on the right path to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
Now, if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so I may turn to the right or the left.”
Then Laban and Bethu’el answered and said, “This matter comes from Yahawah; we cannot speak to you either good or bad.
Behold, Ribqah is before you; take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master’s son, as Yahawah has spoken.”
And when Abaraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself to the earth before Yahawah.
Then the servant brought out silver and gold jewelry, and garments, and gave them to Ribqah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and to her mother.
Then they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they stayed the night.
But her brother and her mother said, “Let the young woman stay with us a few days, at least ten, then she may go.”
But he said to them, “Do not delay me, since Yahawah has made my journey successful. Send me away so that I may go to my master.”
So they said, “Let us call the young woman and ask her.”
And they called Ribqah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” And she said, “I will go.”
So they sent Ribqah their sister away, along with her nurse, Abaraham’s servant, and his men.
They blessed Ribqah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands; may your descendants possess the gates of those who hate them.”
Then Ribqah and her young women arose, mounted the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Ribqah and departed.
Yatschaq had come from the direction of Be’er-Lachay-Ro’i, for he was living in the Negev.
Toward evening Yatschaq went out into the field to meditate. He looked up and saw camels approaching.
And Ribqah lifted her eyes and saw Yatschaq, and she dismounted from the camel.
And she said to the servant, “Who is this man walking in the field to meet us?”
And the servant said, “It is my master.” So she took a veil and covered herself.
And Yatschaq brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Ribqah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. So Yatschaq was comforted after his mother’s death.
And Abaraham took another wife, whose name was Qeturah.
And she bore him Zimran, Yoqshan, Medan, Midyan, Yishbaq, and Shuach.
And Yoqshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were the Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
The sons of Midyan were Ephah, Epher, Chanok, Abida, and Elda’ah. All these were the sons of Qeturah.
And Abaraham gave all that he had to Yatschaq (Isaac).
But to the sons of the concubines that Abaraham had, he gave gifts and sent them away from his son Yatschaq, eastward to the land of the east.
These are the days of the years of Abaraham’s life: 175 years.
Then Abaraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man and satisfied, and he was gathered to his people.
And his sons Yatschaq and Yishma’al buried him in the cave of Makhpelah, in the field of Ephron son of Tsohar the Hittite, which is near Mamre—
The field that Abaraham had purchased from the sons of Heth. There Abaraham was buried, with Sarah his wife.
